# Using Maestro in Kilo Code

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Kilo Code.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.kilocode/skills/maestro/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.kilocode/skills/maestro/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness kilo --skill maestro
node packages/cli install --harness kilo --skill maestro --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Kilo Code loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also name it in the request, for example: "Use the maestro skill to ...".

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.kilocode/skills/maestro` for a project install, or `~/.kilocode/skills/maestro` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Run `kilo debug skill` to list the skills Kilo discovered.

## Notes

- Folders named skills-<mode>, such as skills-code, load only in that mode.
- Maestro delegates every step. Load the model preferences and the provider catalog before choosing a worker. Paseo can drive Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Cline, Cursor, Kilo, Hermes, Antigravity, Muse, and ACP providers. Read references/harness/adapters.md before the first spawn, and record the worker chat id before the first prompt.
- Kilo shares the OpenCode CLI shape: kilo run --session <id> continues the recorded chat, and -m selects the worker model.
- Documentation: [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills) (path source: official).
